title: Good transaction fee disclosure for bank, building society and credit union deposit and payments products (transaction accounts)
subject: This guide addresses the disclosure of transaction fees for retail deposit and payments products (transaction accounts) offered by banks, credit unions and building societies. It aims to improve consumer understanding of fees and promote better disclosure practices by financial institutions.
background: The guide was developed against the backdrop of financial services reforms, the Uniform Consumer Credit Code, and industry codes of conduct. Its purpose is to provide a single reference for institutions and consumers on current legal and self-regulatory fee disclosure requirements, as well as ASIC's views on good practice. It is intended for banks, building societies, credit unions, and consumers of transaction account services.
ruling: ASIC expects institutions to adopt clear, timely, and meaningful fee disclosure practices that enable consumers to manage the cost of their banking. The guide sets out principles for good disclosure, including that fees should be prominently displayed, explained in plain language, and provided before account opening and periodically thereafter. ASIC will monitor the effectiveness of the guide and may make recommendations to the government if there are insufficient signs of improvement. The guide will be reviewed at least every three years and may be amended as needed to reflect changes in legislation or self-regulatory requirements.
